prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, half-length demi statue portrait — a sculpted figure ending at the waist. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to one single, deliberately carved rounded base at her waist, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her waist, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Korean woman in Gangnam-eonni makeup — glowing dewy skin, a precise winged liner, softly defined brown eyeshadow, full natural lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, sculpted contour with a satin highlight, plump glossy rose-coral lips, long sleek chestnut waves, a poised, refined, confident expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a big rose-gold hoop.

Physique: A giantess on an even scale — massive rounded shoulders spanning more than four head-widths, huge thick arms, a colossal full chest, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, no single part standing out.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — both shoulders, both arms and hands, her chest and belly — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically carved from ONE solid block of genuine Brazilian tulipwood, a richly streaked wood in cream, rose-pink and violet tones running in irregular ribbons, polished to a warm satin sheen, completely opaque. It is one continuous sculpted mass, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same wood. At her waist, the whole solid form curves inward evenly on every side and rounds off into one single, smooth, satin-polished base — the wood simply reaching its natural end there, the one rounded base resting flat on the surface beneath her.

Opacity: everything below the collarbones is solid, completely opaque carved tulipwood — no light passes through it at any point. It has the same dense, fibrous solidity throughout, catching light only as soft satin sheen along the grain, never glowing from within. Her face, by contrast, is warm, soft, living flesh, its natural colour nowhere close to the colour of the wood.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the wood's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded base at her waist is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft rose pink on one side and a pale lilac on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a matte dark floor beneath her.

Pose: her left hand (solid material) resting at her waist, her right hand (solid material) held at chest height clear of her body, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so rose-pink light glances off the left half and lilac light glances off the right half, catching in the grain as soft highlights. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
